subject: Open Learning Institute
claim: OIC 1429/1978 designated The Open Learning Institute as a Provincial Institute under the Colleges and Provincial Institutes Act.
locator: PDF p1; approved and ordered 1 June 1978
caveat: Do not substitute a retrospective 6 June date for the original order.

subject: Open Learning Institute
claim: The attached mission covers first degrees in arts/science, career/technical/vocational and adult basic education, delivered by distance with support services.
locator: PDF p2, attached ministerial Statement of Mission

subject: Open Learning Agency Act
claim: The Open Learning Agency Act received assent on 17 December 1987; s23 deferred commencement.
locator: PDF pp1,5; assent heading and s23
caveat: Assent did not itself establish the agency in operation under s2.

subject: Open Learning Agency
claim: OLA Act s2 came into force on 18 January 1988 under BC Reg 14/88 / OIC25/1988, establishing the corporation.
locator: 1987 Act s2; OIC25 clause(a); official 1993 consolidation editorial commencement note after s23
caveat: The 18 January commencement is stated by the official consolidation. The original OIC was approved 14 January; a separate 1988 Gazette deposit page was not recovered.

subject: Open Learning Agency
claim: The Act required OLA to establish three components: open university, open college and knowledge network.
locator: OLA Act s4; commencement note
caveat: This dates the statutory requirement, not evidence that each component began delivering services that day.

subject: Open Learning Agency
claim: The original board consisted of 11 LGIC appointees from ministerial nominees; LGIC appointed one as chair.
locator: OLA Act s5; original commencement
caveat: The 2002 Act later changed the permitted board size. This is the rule at commencement, not a timeless current statement.

subject: Open Learning Institute and Knowledge Network of the West Communications Authority
claim: On 1 April 1988 both predecessors dissolved, their boards ceased, all property and rights vested in OLA, and OLA assumed their debts and obligations subject to preserved creditor rights.
locator: Act s17(1)–(2); OIC25 clause(c)
predecessors: Knowledge Network of the West Communications Authority

subject: Open Learning Institute
claim: OIC357/1988 separately rescinded OLI’s provincial-institute designation effective 1 April 1988.
locator: PDF p1, sole operative paragraph

subject: Open Learning Agency Repeal Act 2002
claim: The 2002 Act authorized a minister-directed winding-up plan or transition administrator; dissolution was contingent on future repeal of OLA Act ss2 and 5. It did not dissolve OLA on assent.
locator: Entire Act, particularly s2 inserting OLA ss19–22 and transitional s3
caveat: No executed 2005 asset-transfer agreement or minister-approved winding-up plan was recovered.

subject: University College of the Cariboo / Thompson Rivers University
claim: TRU Act s2(1) continued University College of the Cariboo as Thompson Rivers University when the whole Act commenced on 31 March 2005.
locator: TRU Act s2(1),31; sole operative clause OIC364/2005; Gazette Reg201/2005
caveat: Institutional accounts use 1 April 2005 for the operating transition. Preserve that separately; do not overwrite the commencement date.

subject: Open University and Open College operations
claim: TRU’s first audited financial statements record acquisition of OLA’s Open University and Open College operations and specified assets and liabilities effective 1 April 2005.
locator: PDF p9 / printed p5, Note1(a)
caveat: This is a partial operational/asset transfer; OLA as a corporation continued and became Knowledge Network Corporation in 2008.

subject: TRU Planning Council for Open Learning
claim: TRU Act s11 established the Planning Council for Open Learning as part of the Act commencing 31 March 2005.
locator: TRU Act ss11–12; Reg201/2005
caveat: Members include ex officio, presidential appointees, nominees, elected teaching staff and a student; it is not an all-Cabinet-appointed board.

subject: Thompson Rivers University
claim: TRU must serve both the region designated by LGIC and the open-learning needs of British Columbia, including degree, postsecondary, adult basic and credit-bank functions.
locator: TRU Act s3; Reg201/2005

subject: Open Learning Agency Repeal Act 2002
claim: Knowledge Network Corporation Act s25 repealed the 2002 OLA Repeal Act on assent, removing its contingent dissolution framework before the OLA Act was repealed in 2008.
locator: Original 2007 Act ss25,27 (PDF pp7–8); TLC row25
caveat: Do not infer dissolution from the title of the 2002 Act or from the later repeal of OLA’s governing Act alone.

subject: Open Learning Agency / Knowledge Network Corporation
claim: OLA was continued as Knowledge Network Corporation under s2(1) on 27 June 2008, when Reg187/2008 took effect and the OLA Act was repealed.
locator: Knowledge Act ss2,19,27; Reg187/2008; TLC
caveat: OLA and Knowledge Network Corporation are one continued corporation; the former Knowledge Network society dissolved into OLA in 1988.

subject: Knowledge Network Corporation
claim: At commencement the Act expressly made the corporation a non-agent of government; LGIC appoints up to 11 directors; the minister may designate the chair, otherwise the board appoints its chair.
locator: ss2(4),5(1)–(4); commencement regulation
caveat: Board appointment, statutory non-agency and fiscal-agent status are separate relations; none alone means a government shareholding.

subject: Knowledge Network Corporation
claim: The statute defines its public-education broadcasting and lifelong-learning purposes as serving British Columbians and collaborating with independent television and web producers.
locator: s4; commencement regulation
